Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Timothy Bentum urges parents to be actively involved in children’s lives to prevent drug abuse Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 17 November 2026 11:30am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Media personality and Lead Pastor of Grace Avenue Ministry, Timothy Bentum, has urged parents to become more actively involved in their children's lives beyond providing financial support, warning that peer pressure and drug abuse continue to threaten the future of young people.
He said many young people were introduced to drugs through friends, making schools and peer groups important spaces for sustained education and intervention.
Speaking ahead of the launch of a five-year senior high school drug prevention initiative, Mr Bentum stressed the importance of helping students make informed decisions about friendships and resist pressure to experiment with substances.
He cautioned that no drug could genuinely improve academic performance or give users lasting confidence without the risk of addiction and its damaging consequences.
"There is no drug that can make you study better or give you confidence without the clap back of getting addicted and then totally throwing away your whole destiny," he said.
Mr Bentum disclosed that the initiative would involve a sustained tour of senior high schools across Ghana's 16 regions, targeting 252 schools over five years.
He explained that the programme would go beyond one-off awareness campaigns by establishing support structures within participating schools to help students struggling with personal challenges, peer pressure and substance abuse.
As part of the intervention, organisers would identify three to four teachers in each school and take them through a short counselling programme to equip them to serve as the first point of contact for students who need guidance or someone to talk to.
He said the approach was intended to ensure that students could access support within their schools rather than struggle with their challenges without assistance.
The pastor also appealed to parents to pay closer attention to their children's emotional and social well-being, arguing that parenting must extend beyond meeting their financial needs.
He said parents needed to be present, build stronger relationships with their children and create an environment in which young people felt comfortable discussing their difficulties.
Mr Bentum emphasised that preventing drug abuse required collective responsibility, urging individuals and the wider society to support efforts aimed at protecting young people.
The initiative is scheduled to be officially launched on Saturday, November 21, at 3:00 p.m. at Christ the King Church.
